claims.text: Mn is magnetically frustrated in equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Magnetic frustration associated with Mn suppresses the dislocation-triggered FCC-to-HCP transformation in Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni relative to CrCoNi.
A deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation is active in equiatomic CrCoNi.
The same transformation mechanism is active generally in Mn-reduced quaternary or ternary derivatives of the quinary alloy.
CrCoNi and Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni can both have single-phase FCC starting structures.
The compared specimens have been produced through identical thermomechanical processing and have otherwise comparable initial microstructures.
The controlled intervention is uniaxial tensile testing at the same temperature and strain rate for all alloys.
The FCC-to-HCP transformation is triggered by dislocation slip and interactions with internal boundaries.
Moderate-to-high tensile strains activate the proposed transformation-induced plasticity mechanism.
The structural mediator consists of nanometer-scale HCP regions at slip bands or internal boundaries.
Removing Mn reduces magnetic frustration and permits a magnetically tunable FCC-to-HCP transformation in CrCoNi.
The deformation-induced transformation increases strength without compromising plastic deformation in CrCoNi.
The transformation increases strain hardening and delays localized necking.
Suppressing the transformation in the quinary alloy changes its dislocation and twinning behavior.
Relative to equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni, CrCoNi should show more HCP formation during deformation.
Relative to the quinary baseline, Mn-free or Mn-reduced alloys should have higher strain hardening, strength, and ductility.
The hypothesis applies when dislocation motion dominates and thermally activated magnetic ordering can influence phase stability.
The alloy comparison differs primarily in Mn content.
The quantitative effect of magnetic frustration on the mechanically loaded FCC-to-HCP energy barrier is not yet established.
Failure to observe significantly greater HCP formation or distinguishable strain hardening and mechanical performance in the Mn-free or Mn-reduced alloy would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The comparison is said to differ primarily in Mn content, but replacing equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni with equiatomic CrCoNi removes both Mn and Fe and changes the atomic fractions of Cr, Co, and Ni. Thus the proposed comparison does not isolate Mn content.
